title: Le R français
intro: The French **R** /ʁ/ is made at the back of the mouth, not with the tip of the tongue. It's softer than people think: a light scrape of air, like a quiet gargle. Get it right and you'll sound French straight away.

cases.label: how to make it
cases.rule: Keep the tip of your tongue **down**, behind your bottom teeth. Raise the **back** of your tongue, as for /ɡ/, but don't close: let the air scrape through gently.

cases.label: R at the start: rue, rire
cases.rule: At the start of a word: *rue, rouge, rire, rond, rapide*. No English *r*: *rue* is not *roo*!

cases.label: R between vowels: Paris
cases.rule: Between two vowels the R is light and short: *Paris, arriver, heureux*.

cases.label: R after a consonant: trois, grand
cases.rule: After a consonant, say both sounds together, with no vowel in between: *trois, grand, prendre, frère, crêpe*.

cases.label: R at the end: bonjour, noir
cases.rule: At the end of a word the R is usually **pronounced**, softly: *bonjour, noir, sœur, mer, partir*.

cases.label: the silent R of -er
cases.rule: In most words ending in **-er**, the R is silent: *parler, manger, premier, boulanger* (/e/). Also **monsieur** /mə.sjø/.

cases.label: one R can change the word
cases.rule: Forget the R and you say another word: *toi / trois, fait / frais, bas / bar, gant / grand*.

sections.title: 1. How to make the French R
text: Say **/ɡa/** and feel where the back of your tongue touches. Now make it touch *less* and let the air rub through: that's the French R. The tip of your tongue stays down, behind your bottom teeth.
sections.tip: Practise slowly: *a-ra, a-ra*. Keep it light, like a whisper in your throat, not a growl!

sections.title: 2. At the start of a word
4. After a consonant
text: Don't put a little vowel between the consonant and the R: **trois** is one syllable, /tʁwa/.

sections.title: 5. At the end of a word
sections.tip: The final R is soft and short: don't drop it, but don't growl it either.

sections.title: 6. The silent R of -er
text: In infinitives and in most words ending in **-er**, the R is silent: **-er** sounds /e/.
sections.tip: Exceptions: short words like **mer, fer, hiver, cher** do say the R: /mɛʁ/, /ʃɛʁ/.

sections.title: 7. One R can change the word

story.title: Le petit rat de Paris
story.en: Grandpa Jacques tells Lou a bedtime story full of R sounds.

lines.fr: Grand-père Jacques raconte une histoire à Lou :
lines.en: Grandpa Jacques tells Lou a story:

lines.fr: « Il était une fois, à {Paris|r-middle}, un petit {rat|r-start} très {rapide|r-start}.
lines.en: “Once upon a time, in Paris, there was a very fast little rat.

lines.fr: Il habitait dans une {rue|r-start} calme, avec ses {trois frères|r-cluster} et sa {sœur|r-end}.
lines.en: He lived in a quiet street, with his three brothers and his sister.

lines.fr: Un matin, il est entré chez le {boulanger|r-silent} : « {Bonjour|r-end}, {monsieur|r-silent} ! »
lines.en: One morning, he went into the baker's: “Good morning, sir!”

lines.fr: Mais le boulanger avait un {grand|r-cluster} chat {noir|r-end}…
lines.en: But the baker had a big black cat…

lines.fr: Le petit rat a couru, couru, couru… Enfin, il est {arrivé|r-middle} chez lui, très {heureux|r-middle}.
lines.en: The little rat ran, and ran, and ran… At last, he got home, very happy.

lines.fr: Sa sœur a ri : « {Toi|r-pairs} ? Tu as peur d'un chat ? »
lines.en: His sister laughed: “You? You're scared of a cat?”

lines.fr: « Moi ? Non… J'ai peur de {trois|r-pairs} chats ! »
lines.en: “Me? No… I'm scared of three cats!”

lines.fr: Depuis ce jour, le petit rat {préfère|r-cluster} manger son fromage à la maison, avec ses frères. »
lines.en: Since that day, the little rat prefers to eat his cheese at home, with his brothers.”

lines.fr: Elle veut dire « {Merci, grand-père|r-how} »… mais le R français, c'est difficile à trois ans !
lines.en: She wants to say “Thank you, Grandpa”… but the French R is hard when you're three!

quiz.q: Where do you make the French R?
options: at the back of the mouth
with the tip of the tongue
quiz.answer: at the back of the mouth

quiz.q: When you say the French R, the tip of your tongue…
options: stays down, behind the bottom teeth
touches the roof of the mouth
quiz.answer: stays down, behind the bottom teeth

quiz.q: How many R sounds are there in « heureux »?
In « frère », « prendre », « trois », the R comes…
options: right after a consonant: say them together
at the end of the word
quiz.answer: right after a consonant: say them together
